messages:
sylvia: Quick q — tenant feature flags (regional_fallback_enabled) interacting weirdly with hedging windows. Seeing double hedges when the flag flips mid-request. Anyone else?

mike: yup saw that in canary yesterday, seemed like a race between routing decision cache and the feature flag refresh.

arya: can you paste a small repro or trace id? might be the decision cache TTL + feature flag change -> policy eval path thinks route not compatible then later hedges.

sylvia: trace: rtx-7c9f, snippet below. essentially: request hits edge -> policy eval picks primary region -> feature flag flips -> fallback path chosen -> hedger fires because primary still in-flight.

sylvia: ```
policy: {
  tenant_id: t-123,
  allow_regional_fallback: true,
  hedging: { window_ms: 60 }
}
```

jordan: That makes sense. Right now policy eval is memoized per-request id during a single request lifetime but feature flags come from a separate service with eventual consistency. If flag changes mid-flight we don't re-eval. Leads to mixed signals.

kevin: Options: 1) make feature flags part of the policy evaluation input (immutable for request) 2) add a short feature-flag-stable window (e.g. don't re-eval for X ms) 3) make hedger consult the last-known policy decision rather than re-evaluating compatibility on fallback.

mike: tradeoffs: (1) is safest for determinism but requires plumbing flags into request context everywhere (perf cost, more data on wire). (2) is easiest but may mask legitimate fast toggles (compliance toggles). (3) is cheap but could mis-route if policy changed for good reason.

arya: performance numbers: adding 1 extra small map (flags blob ~200 bytes) to request context adds ~0.5% p99 latency in our bench. Not huge but nonzero.

sylvia: Our SLOs are tight. I'm leaning toward (1) but maybe with optional sampling for older tenants to avoid perf costs. Thoughts?

devx-bot: FYI — adding request-scoped flags will require SDK updates for node/python/go; will add ~2 days per SDK to ship if we go that route.

jordan: Another hybrid: include a feature-flag hash in the request context (small 8 bytes). Router can check hash equality to detect if flag set changed and decide to honor original decision. That keeps wire small.

kevin: good idea. hash approach preserves determinism without full payload. but needs consistent hashing of flags and stable key derivation. Also rollout complexity when new flags appear.

mike: Edge case: if operator flips a global compliance flag (must_disable_fallback) we probably need immediate effect. We should allow an override path that short-circuits memoization for admin-level flags.

arya: Agree. Let's classify flags into: admin-critical (immediate), tenant-stable (tied to request), and telemetry-only (no routing effect). Policy engine can treat admin-critical as always authoritative and cause reeval.

sylvia: Proposal: implement flag-hash in request metadata + SDK changes to compute it. Policy engine uses (request_id, flag-hash) as cache key. Add blacklist of admin flags that force reeval. Hedger consults cached decision; fallback policy uses cached decision for compatibility checks.

jordan: Implementation notes: need to update ingress sidecar to compute hash before policy call. Also update policy-cache key derivation from: (request_id) -> (request_id, flag-hash). Backfill for existing cache entries? probably not necessary; stale semantics ok during rollout.

devx-bot: Checklist: SDK updates, sidecar change, policy-service cache-key bump, tests for race scenario, release notes.

mike: Can someone sketch the cache-key change patch? small pseudo: 
```
// old
cache_key = request_id
// new
cache_key = request_id + '|' + flag_hash
```

kevin: remember to limit flag_hash length in logs. Don't print raw flags.

arya: I'll take the patch for policy-service + tests. sylvia can you handle sidecar change? mike can you coordinate SDK owners?

sylvia: yep I'll own sidecar.

mike: I'll ping SDK leads.

kevin: We should add a short sim in policy-sandbox to model flip mid-flight and ensure hedger doesn't double-fire.

arya: will add sim test. Also add a small perf regression run after SDK + sidecar changes.

sylvia: timeline? aim for small canary next week.

mike: SGTM. Final question — do we want a feature gate to enable flag-hash behavior per-tenant so we can opt-in?

jordan: yes, opt-in makes rollout safer. Default off, enable for high-usage tenants first.

ops-bot: NOTE: Created task INF-8272 "Implement flag-hash routing stability" and assigned to arya, sylvia, mike.

sylvia: thanks all. I'll post a short RFC PR with the design and a sample rollout plan. :thumbsup:
